items.title: fix(team-controller): native update backups from failed or recovered …
items.summary: fix(team-controller): native update backups from failed or recovered deployments are never retired (#185600) * fix(team-controller): retire settled native update backups during release pruning Schema-crossing deployments create a per-transaction root under `/.openclaw-update/` where the candidate's `update migrate` writes its pre-migration snapshot and receipt. Only `update finish` on an accepted deployment removed the snapshot; restored rollbacks, forward recovery, migrations that died before their receipt, and early failures left their roots forever. Release pruning now settles them. While any activation journal exists, nothing is retired. Otherwise roots whose receipt is absent (Doctor never ran), `migrated`, `restored`, or `finished` are retired; `backed-up`, `failed`, `restoring-config`, and unreadable receipts stay with a RETAIN line. The current deployment keeps its own root until the next prune. The runtime account, which owns these trees, removes their contents; root only removes the emptied directory. Release-note context: the Team deployment controller now retires native update backups of settled transactions during release pruning. * fix(team-controller): run native backup removal from an accessible directory A real-account proof (real runuser and a separate runtime account) showed GNU find, run as the runtime account, refuses to start from a working directory only root can enter. Team runs deployments from root-private scripts, so every settled native root would have been retained instead of retired. The runtime-account removal now runs from /.
